item.text: {"question_id":"4B.1","answer":"During Lula’s 2023 period, the evidence shows formal continuity of the electoral and constitutional order: Congress conducted the presidential inauguration, and Lula assumed office through the recorded transfer-of-power ceremony (BATCH-0013-E002; BATCH-0003-E001). The TCU later reported no material discrepancies in its audit of the 2022 electronic-voting process, but this was an institutional finding about the electoral system and does not demonstrate a Lula-directed reform or that his party could readily lose (BATCH-0015-E005). When Bolsonaro supporters attacked state institutions while rejecting Lula’s electoral victory, Lula ordered federal intervention in Federal District security and called for punishment, indicating resistance to an attempted extra-constitutional reversal (BATCH-0009-E010; BATCH-0017-E013). Subsequent accountability was principally judicial rather than personally directed by Lula (BATCH-0001-E004; BATCH-0003-E006; BATCH-0003-E007). The record also contains unresolved disputes about intelligence, deployment, inherited security personnel, and preservation of some images; these qualify assessment of implementation and attribution but do not establish that Lula himself obstructed contestability (BATCH-0020-E017; BATCH-0020-E018; BATCH-0020-E021; BATCH-0020-E025; BATCH-0020-E026). No supplied evidence documents Lula accepting a verified opposition victory during the target period or comprehensive Lula-attributable electoral-administration changes. Overall, the evidence supports constitutional and electoral continuity and defense against an attempted repudiation of the 2022 result, but is insufficient to establish the broader standard of making power genuinely contestable through Lula-specific reforms or demonstrated acceptance of an opposition
